classification.difficultyReason: Translate Mary’s turn number into the number of preceding misses by both players, then include her immediate win when adding the three mutually exclusive winning sequences.

content.prompt: Bob and Mary roll a die in turns, and the game is won by the first person to roll the number six. Mary rolls first. Find the probability that Mary wins

answer.worked:
Mary and Bob each miss a six on their first roll, then Mary rolls a six. The rolls are independent.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{Mary wins on turn 2})&=\frac{5}{6}\times\frac{5}{6}\times\frac{1}{6}\\P(\text{Mary wins on turn 2})&=\frac{25}{216}\end{align*}$$

The first four rolls must all miss a six. Mary then rolls a six on the fifth roll.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{Mary wins on turn 3})&=\left(\frac{5}{6}\right)^4\times\frac{1}{6}\\P(\text{Mary wins on turn 3})&=\frac{625}{7776}\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$\frac{2821}{7776}$

Add the probabilities of Mary winning on her first, second or third turn.
answer.worked:
Mary wins on her first turn if she rolls a six immediately. The three possible winning turns are mutually exclusive. Let $W$ be the event that Mary wins within her first three turns.

$$\begin{align*}P(W)&=\frac{1}{6}+\frac{25}{216}+\frac{625}{7776}\\P(W)&=\frac{1296+900+625}{7776}\\P(W)&=\frac{2821}{7776}\end{align*}$$
